claim: Candidate A of the ADR-0012 exact-pin decision spike (a minimal upstream/fork patch that accepts controller-issued writer and compactor epochs) is implemented against the pinned crates.io slatedb 0.15.0, builds, and its qualifying matrix passes; the mutant that restores internal observe-and-bind allocation is killed by three of the five new cases.
status: candidate implemented and measured - NOT the normative decision

fork_form.kind: patch series over the pinned crate

correction_to_the_staged_design.assumed: docs/design/slatedb-external-epochs.md staged the fork as having to build exact-epoch claiming on top of FenceableTransactionalObject, describing external issuance as something upstream lacks.
correction_to_the_staged_design.measured: slatedb-txn-obj 0.15.0 already exports FenceableTransactionalObject::init_with_epoch as a PUBLIC function with exactly the required fail-closed semantics (epoch <= stored -> Fenced before any write), and slatedb already uses it internally for the compactions object (compactions_store.rs, compactor_state_protocols.rs).
correction_to_the_staged_design.consequence: The fork is wiring, not mechanism: five files, ~300 added lines, about half of them tests. This materially lowers the cost and the upstreamability risk of Candidate A and must be weighed in the ADR-0012 decision rather than left as a design assumption.

compiles; the production-lane refusal branch is live

executed.command: MUTANT: init_writer_with_epoch reverted to FenceableTransactionalObject::init (observe-and-bind restored, external argument ignored)
executed.reading: Deliberate and load-bearing: internal allocation still provides mutual exclusion, so the fencing cases survive. A mutant that killed all five would mean the tests were testing fencing, not external issuance.
